messages:
nikhil: quick spike idea: we should validate existing safetensors checkpoints by backfilling the tensor-index sidecar and verifying offsets + checksums. found a few exporters that reorder tensors which breaks simple range-read assumptions. want to align on validator strategy.

tara: ugh. reordering exporters are the worst. how do you detect reorder without materializing the whole file?

evan: parse header once to enumerate tensor metadata. for big files we can stream headers (they're at the start) and build index cheaply. but some gzipped exports put headers at the end or wrap in tar.gz which complicates streaming.

nikhil: noted. spike plan: 1) implement an indexer that supports raw safetensors, gzipped-safetensors, and tar-wrapped shards. 2) compare computed tensor offsets to existing sidecar (if present) and produce a diff report. 3) mark mismatched checkpoints "index-mismatch" and surface to catalog.

tara: what about checkpoints already in the catalog with derived artifacts? if index mismatches we risk invalidating derived compact headers. need a conservative policy.

evan: policy suggestion: do not auto-delete derived artifacts. instead mark derived as "needs-reverify" and add a rederive job queue. runtime treats "needs-reverify" as lower priority and may opt to fallback.

indexer-bot: spike: started job 4467003456-indexer-spike on cluster-2 (10 secs). will attempt sample of 50 popular models.

nikhil: for gzipped / tar cases we'll attempt three strategies: 1) try streaming decompression and parse headers, 2) if headers buried, do a lightweight full-file scan to find header magic, 3) fallback to full download for validation. we should track cost per-checkpoint.

tara: how do we compute consistent checksums? per-tensor sha256 computed during index. but compressed vs uncompressed bytes differ. need to canonicalize to in-memory tensor bytes before hashing. that forces decompression.

evan: yes we need tensor-canonical-digest = sha256(decompressed-tensor-bytes). indexer will compute that. catalog will store both object-level digest and per-tensor canonical digest when available.

sre-ops: watch out for IO storms. if we schedule background reindex for thousands of large checkpoints, S3 egress and staging workers will explode. add rate-limiting and dry-run first.

ikhil: agreed. spike will limit to top-50 and use a single worker. if results useful we design a backfill scheduler with concurrency caps and a token bucket per-bucket.

tara: UX: add a short "index_validation_report" URL in checkpoint metadata with counts: tensors_verified, tensors_missing, reorder_detected, checksum_mismatches, actions_recommended. make it accessible to solutions engs.

evan: edgecase: exporters that pack multiple models into one file (rare) - indexer should detect multiple header segments and bail with a special code so humans can inspect.

ikhil: ok actionable: evan will build the indexer spike that handles raw/gzip/tar. tara will draft catalog flags + report schema. I'll wire a small UI in the catalog to surface reports. we'll constrain concurrency.

indexer-bot: spike completed: 50 models scanned, 7 had reorder or checksum issues. report URLs: https://catalog/reports/4467003456/ (internal).

tara: nice. can you attach a sample diff for one model? want to see what reorder looks like.

evan: one sample: tensor order in safetensors header was [wte,ln1,w1,ln2,w2] but a particular exporter wrote [wte,w1,ln1,w2,ln2]. offsets still valid but tensor-boundaries moved -> per-tensor read_window incorrect. diff shows new offsets + canonical sha mismatch for 2 tensors.

ikhil: thanks. next steps: incorporate decompression-canonicalization in ingest staging for new uploads to avoid future mismatches. also add a signer check that index signature implies canonicalization performed.

sre-ops: please add backfill schedule that runs at low-traffic hours and a kill-switch for any bucket causing >x errors.

tara: will add the report schema and migration steps to the ingest RFC. evan, ping me when spike code is in so I can consume reports.

evan: will do, pushing spike PR shortly.

ikhil: thanks all, this uncovered exporter weirdness. we'll fold findings into the RFC and plan a cautious backfill.
